sections.title: What You Are Learning
paragraphs: AWS networking questions become easier when you identify whether the requirement involves isolation, a VPC component, traffic security, DNS, or connectivity to AWS.
sections.callout: Do I need to isolate, divide, protect, resolve, or connect the network?

sections.title: AWS Network Services
paragraphs: AWS network services provide isolation, addressing, connectivity, routing, traffic delivery, and name resolution for cloud resources and connected environments.
sections.callout: First identify the networking job, then select the service or control.

sections.title: Amazon VPC
paragraphs: Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (Amazon VPC) lets customers define a logically isolated virtual network for AWS resources. Customers choose address ranges, subnets, routes, gateways, and security controls.
sections.callout: Logically isolated AWS network → Amazon VPC

sections.title: Subnets
paragraphs: A subnet is an IP address range within a VPC. Each subnet resides in one Availability Zone and provides a placement boundary for resources.
sections.callout: IP range within a VPC and one AZ → Subnet

sections.title: VPC Gateways
paragraphs: Gateway components create connectivity paths between a VPC and destinations such as the internet, other networks, or supported AWS services.
sections.callout: Network entrance or exit path → Gateway

sections.title: Security in a VPC
paragraphs: Customers combine security groups, network ACLs, routing, monitoring, and supported security services to control and evaluate network traffic.

entries.title: Security Groups
paragraphs: Stateful virtual firewalls that control allowed inbound and outbound traffic for associated resources.

entries.title: Network ACLs
paragraphs: Stateless traffic filters applied at the subnet boundary.

entries.title: Amazon Inspector
paragraphs: Evaluates supported workloads for vulnerabilities and can identify unintended network exposure.

sections.title: Security Group vs. Network ACL

table.caption: Separate the two common VPC traffic controls
rows: Stateless filter at the subnet boundary

sections.callout: RESOURCE + STATEFUL = SECURITY GROUP · SUBNET + STATELESS = NACL

sections.title: Amazon Route 53
paragraphs: Amazon Route 53 is a scalable Domain Name System (DNS) web service that directs users to applications and other resources.
sections.callout: DNS or domain-name routing → Amazon Route 53

sections.title: Connectivity Options to AWS
paragraphs: Connectivity choices depend on bandwidth, latency consistency, security, resilience, deployment time, and cost.

entries.title: AWS VPN
paragraphs: Uses encrypted tunnels to connect users or networks to AWS over an existing network path such as the internet.
entries.memoryHook: Encrypted tunnel over an existing path.

entries.title: AWS Direct Connect
paragraphs: Provides a dedicated private network connection between a customer location and AWS.

sections.title: AWS VPN vs. AWS Direct Connect

table.caption: Choose the connection based on the requirement
rows: Encrypted tunnel over an existing network such as the internet

sections.title: GSA Scenario Recognition
bullets: Create an isolated AWS network → Amazon VPC
Place resources in an IP range inside one AZ → Subnet
Control stateful traffic for a resource → Security group
Filter stateless traffic at a subnet boundary → Network ACL
Assess workload vulnerabilities and network exposure → Amazon Inspector
Route a domain name to an application → Route 53
Encrypted connection over the internet → AWS VPN
Dedicated private connection → AWS Direct Connect
sections.callout: The boundary and connection type reveal the answer.

entries.title: VPC vs. Subnet
paragraphs: VPC → isolated virtual network. Subnet → IP range inside the VPC and one Availability Zone.

entries.title: Security Group vs. Network ACL
paragraphs: Security group → stateful and resource-associated. Network ACL → stateless and subnet boundary.

entries.title: Route 53 Trap
paragraphs: Route 53 is the DNS service; the number in its name does not make it a generic routing-table service.

entries.title: VPN vs. Direct Connect
paragraphs: VPN → encrypted tunnel over an existing path. Direct Connect → dedicated private link.

entries.title: Inspector vs. Traffic Filter
paragraphs: Inspector assesses supported workloads for vulnerabilities and exposure; it is not the firewall controlling each connection.

Vulnerability and exposure assessment → Amazon Inspector
Dedicated private link → AWS Direct Connect
